full.description: This is a diagrammatic illustration depicting the stages of cellular apoptosis. It shows a normal cell transitioning through membrane blebbing and nuclear fragmentation. Eventually, the cell breaks down into apoptotic bodies containing intact organelles. This represents the programmed cell death process in a mammalian cell.

blind.description: This image is a photomicrograph of lung tissue showing a fully formed granuloma. The central area is composed of granular caseation necrosis, which is surrounded by epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, and a peripheral rim of lymphocytes bounded by fibroblasts. These findings are characteristic of a necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, most commonly associated with tuberculosis.

random.description: This image is a diagram illustrating the process of apoptosis, or programmed cell death. It shows a normal cell undergoing morphological changes, including cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, and the formation of apoptotic bodies. These sequential stages depict the controlled breakdown of a dying cell. The diagram clearly outlines the cellular mechanisms involved in this vital biological process.
